$why: The exec baseline W5's '2 processes per Bash tool call' target is defined against.

It did not exist until 2026-09-09: W5 P0 lists a fork counter as a deliverable and W5 P6 records '456 execs per Bash call to 35', and on 2026-09-09 `grep -rlnP 'strace|GUARD_PASS|HOOKS_ONLY|FORK_COUNT' .ci .claude scripts` returned ZERO files while `git ls-files | grep -iE 'strace|exec-baseline'` returned zero as well. Both numbers were unreproducible.

Every number below is DERIVED from .claude/settings.json by .claude/rediacc_hooks/execcount.py and pinned here. It counts the processes the HARNESS starts (one per hooks[].command), which is a floor on the true exec count and never the whole of it: in-guard forks are a separate measurement this file does not make.

Enforced by check:ci-hook-exec-baseline, which fails in BOTH directions. A count that GREW is a refusal. A count that SHRANK is also a refusal, saying so and printing the new value to paste, because a baseline that silently absorbs an improvement stops being able to prove the next one.

target.why: W5's stated target, recorded here so the gap is a number rather than a memory. Today's value is in measured.tools.Bash; the gate does NOT enforce the target, it enforces that today's value cannot drift without an edit here. D4 (lifecycle collapse 30 -> 11) moved it on 2026-09-21, from 12 to 3: one harness command per (event, matcher) pattern, with the commands each pattern used to register now listed in .claude/rediacc_hooks/lifecycle.py. The remaining 3 are the PreToolUse chain head and the two PostToolUse entries.

probeTools.AskUserQuestion: the third PreToolUse matcher. Its chain is the shortest, which makes it the row that notices a guard being added to every chain by habit.
probeTools.Bash: the tool W5's '2 processes per Bash tool call' target is stated about. This row IS the target, and it is 3 today, down from 12 at the D4 collapse.
probeTools.BashOutput: not a matcher, a PROBE for the unanchored `Bash` matcher. It is the one tool in this table whose two readings disagree; see ambiguousMatchers.
probeTools.Glob: a read-only tool no PreToolUse matcher names. Its row is the cost of the three wildcard PostToolUse entries and nothing else, so it is the floor every tool pays.
probeTools.NotebookEdit: inside the anchored Edit-family alternation. The rarest of the four, which is why it is listed rather than assumed to track Edit.
probeTools.Read: the highest-frequency tool in a session, and the floor row that a new wildcard PostToolUse entry would move first.
probeTools.Task: a subagent launch. Listed because a hook added here multiplies by the number of subagents, not by the number of turns.
probeTools.TodoWrite: a wildcard-only tool whose name contains `Write`; it is the anchored-alternation counterpart of BashOutput and it is NOT ambiguous, which is the evidence that anchoring is what removes the ambiguity.

BashOutput.why: BLOCKER: the `Bash` matcher in .claude/settings.json is written bare, not anchored, and nothing in this repository documents whether the harness matches a matcher with search or with fullmatch. Under search, `Bash` selects `BashOutput` and every Bash-chain guard runs on a BashOutput call; under fullmatch it does not. The two readings differ by 2 processes, down from 9 before the D4 collapse; the ambiguity itself is unchanged, only its cost. This is pinned rather than resolved because resolving it means either reading the harness or anchoring the matcher to `^Bash$`, and anchoring it is a behaviour change to every Bash guard that belongs in its own box with its own evidence. It shrinks by anchoring the matcher, never by editing this list.
